newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: BNFL, Cogema deny breaking vow to South Africa.
newsitem.headline: BNFL, Cogema deny breaking vow to South Africa.

text.p: British and French companies that shipped radioactive nuclear waste past the South African coast this month denied on Wednesday they had broken promises over the route the ship would take.

South African Environmental Affairs Minister Pallo Jordan said last week British Nuclear Fuels (BNFL) and Cogema had assured him the ship, the Pacific Teal, would remain outside the 200-mile exclusive economic zone.
He said the ship had approached to within 90 miles of the coast, and this broken promise would influence South Africa's attitude to future shipments.
But BNFL and Cogema said in a joint statement issued in Cape Town that they had promised only that the ship would not enter South Africa's territorial waters.
"South Africa's territorial waters extend 12 miles from its coastline. That commitment was honoured," the statement said.
The Pacific Teal was carrying used nuclear fuel in vitrified form back to Japan from France, where it had been reprocessed. The reprocessing contract envisages about 30 such shipments.
There was no immediate comment from Jordan's office on the statement.
